factual_claims.claim: OpenAI reported in July 2026 that over the preceding six months, the share of research compute devoted to internal coding inference grew 100-fold, indicating a dramatic increase in the value of AI in research and development.
In America, at least 20 data center projects were canceled in the first three months of 2026 due to local pushback, contributing to $85 billion worth of canceled projects over the past three years.
Favaro and Clark (2026) report that the number of lines of code merged per engineer per day rose roughly 8X between 2024 and Q2 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Empirical measurements from METR's expenditure horizon studies show that returns to spending additional inference compute on agents performing frontier optimization tasks diminish rapidly, with performance plateauing in the low thousands of dollars per run.

Gundlach et al. (2025) demonstrate that standard baseline models treating algorithmic progress as scale-neutral are misspecified because historical algorithmic improvements in machine learning have been largely biased toward large training scales.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A Belief within safetyist and accelerationist discourse that models narrow algorithmic efficiency gains separately from broad economic capability growth. Encompasses: Narrow capability loops, broad economic output passthrough, superelasticity conditions. Excludes: Aggregate capability scaling models.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document introduces a formal distinction between narrow capabilities that optimize algorithmic efficiency and coding tasks, and broad capabilities that drive general economic output. It establishes that narrow self-sustaining acceleration does not necessitate broad capability acceleration unless specific superelasticity conditions are met.
unmapped_concepts.reason: Existing taxonomy nodes cover general capability scaling but lack formal economic modeling of the divergence between narrow algorithmic R&D improvements and broad macroeconomic impacts.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that models artificial intelligence research input through an aggregate function combining human labor, inference compute, and experimental compute. Encompasses: R&D effort aggregators, input cost shares, elasticity of research. Excludes: Single-input scaling laws.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The text modifies standard bottlenecks models by assuming an R&D effort aggregator that combines human researchers, automated AI researchers running on inference compute, and experimental compute into a single scalar input for algorithmic improvement.
unmapped_concepts.reason: Captures the specific methodological approach of combining heterogeneous R&D inputs via cost-share elasticities to estimate recursive self-improvement takeoff conditions.
